entities.name: Filippo Maria Visconti
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Filippo Maria Visconti (1392–1447) was the second and last Duke of Milan from the male line of the venerable Visconti dynasty, reigning from 1412 until his death. His rule marked a critical period of recovery and consolidation for the Duchy of Milan after the fragmentation that followed his father Gian Galeazzo Visconti's death. Operating from his capital in Milan, Visconti skillfully navigated the complex political landscape of 15th-century Italy, restoring much of his family's territorial dominion and establishing a powerful, albeit often feared, state that profoundly influenced the balance of power among the Italian city-states during the early Renaissance. His reign laid the groundwork for the subsequent Sforza dynasty, directly impacting the trajectory of Lombardy and wider Italian politics.

Upon inheriting a fragmented duchy at the age of 20 following the assassination of his brother Giovanni Maria Visconti, Filippo Maria immediately set about reasserting Milanese authority. He employed a succession of brilliant *condottieri*, notably Francesco Bussone da Carmagnola and later Francesco Sforza, to reconquer lost territories including Genoa, Brescia, and Parma. Despite his military successes, Visconti rarely led armies in person, preferring to govern from within the Castello Sforzesco, cultivating a reputation for extreme reclusiveness and paranoia. His strategic alliances and diplomatic maneuvering, often characterized by duplicity, allowed him to expand Milanese influence across Lombardy and beyond, frequently engaging in wars against Venice and Florence, such as the Wars in Lombardy (1423-1454).
